question: Should slow `socket.drain` subscribers receive a bounded reliable control event, or be disconnected and required to resynchronize authoritative session state?
rationale: The current implementation promises deterministic teardown notification but closes overloaded recipients before sending; selecting the intended delivery and recovery guarantee requires Gateway owner judgment.

options.title: Bounded reliable drain
options.body: Add a dedicated bounded control-event delivery mechanism and prove drain receipt under backpressure.

options.title: Disconnect and resynchronize
options.body: Keep close-on-slow semantics, document them publicly, and prove every affected client reloads authoritative session state after reconnect.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Retain existing refresh or polling behavior until a general control-event recovery design is available.

recommendation.title: Bounded reliable drain
recommendation.body: Add a dedicated bounded control-event delivery mechanism and prove drain receipt under backpressure.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current slow-consumer broadcaster contract and has the strongest current-main history across the affected Gateway surface.
